description: A relative of the pink peppercorn tree, but native to the rioplatense region specifically rather than the Andes. Evergreen, so it holds cover all year.
nativeStatus: Native to the Río de la Plata region
nativeRange: Argentina, Uruguay and nearby South America
ecology: Evergreen woody habitat that adds year-round shelter and a long fruiting season to a native planting.
wildlifeNotes: The berries are eaten by more than twenty bird species, and the evergreen canopy provides cover through winter.
size: Altura / height: 2-7 m. Porte: árbol bajo o arbolito, perenne, de copa irregular.
edibleUses: The berries can be used as a pepper substitute.
medicinalUses: Indigenous peoples used the resin as an antiseptic and for dental pain.
